body_markdown:
We haven’t[seen a German vehicle](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/final-parking-space/final-parking-space-1993-volkswagen-eurovan-gl-manual/) in this series for nearly six months, so I decided it was time for an all-time *Legendäre deutsche Maschine* . I found this W124 wagon a couple of years ago at[a Denver-area car graveyard](https://www.pyp.com/locations/co/aurora/11602-e-33rd-avenue/) , and I’ve been saving these photos for a special occasion, i.e., today.


Daimler-Benz


For those who want to be pedantic about Mercedes-Benz terminology, we’ll get two terms that I’ll be using sort-of-incorrectly out of the way now. First, because this car is a wagon, its chassis designation code was *S* 124, not *W* 124; because even most diehard Mercedes-Benz fanatics now refer to every member of the family as a W124, that’s what I’m doing here. Second, Daimler-Benz didn’t make the E-Class name official until 1993, so even though the W124 became an E-Class the moment the suits in Stuttgart so decreed, we must backdate five years to apply it to *this* car.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The W124 had a tough act to follow, and that’s putting it mildly.[Its W123 predecessor](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/innovation/milestones/model-ranges/50-years-of-w-123/) earned a reputation as one of the best-built motor vehicles in human history, especially in Europe, and there was just no way that Daimler-Benz could outdo[that feat](https://www.bbc.com/travel/article/20210819-merci-dix-a-swansong-for-moroccos-mercedes-grand-taxis) while keeping up with cutting-edge technology and staying competitive with Japanese manufacturers on price at the same time.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


I’ve[documented plenty](https://www.murileemartin.com/Junkyard/JunkyardGallery-Mercedes.html) of discarded W123 proto-E-Classes over the years, including a couple[with final odometer readings of more than 400,000 miles](https://www.murileemartin.com/Junkyard/JunkyardGallery-300kMileCars.html) .


Daimler-Benz


As it turned out,[the W124](https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/innovation/milestones/model-ranges/e-clsss-series-w-124/) established nearly as strong a reputation for reliability as its predecessor. It was built from 1985 through 1997 and sold in the United States for the 1986 through 1995 model years.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


You’ll still find plenty of W124 survivors on roads all over the world. I shot this diesel sedan[in Bulgaria](https://www.theautopian.com/why-im-flying-to-junkyards-around-the-world-to-buy-the-most-useless-part-of-any-car/) a couple of years ago.


Daimler-Benz


Naturally, taxi companies in Europe went for the W124 in a big way.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The station wagon version didn’t show up in American Mercedes-Benz dealerships until the 1987 model year, and then only with turbodiesel power.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


For 1988, the oil-burner in the U.S.-market W124 wagon was replaced by a 3.0-liter SOHC straight-six gasoline-burner rated at 177 horsepower and 188 lb.-ft. of torque.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


W124 buyers in the United States could get a sedan with a manual transmission for the first few years, but an overwhelming absence of demand axed that option here. After that, Americans who wanted a new W124 with three pedals had to visit the gray market.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Station wagons were falling out of favor as the 1990s approached, due to competition from the new breeds of[fuel-efficient minivans](https://www.autoweek.com/car-life/a64168807/1984-dodge-caravan-junkyard-treasure/) and[tough-looking SUVs](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/final-parking-space/final-parking-space-1984-jeep-cherokee-chief/) (the year of Peak Wagon in the United States is a tie between 1964 and 1977, according to[exhaustive research on the subject](https://www.autoweek.com/car-life/classic-cars/a39372850/what-year-was-peak-wagon-in-america/) ). Even so, we can *still* buy[a new Mercedes-Benz E-Class wagon](https://www.mbusa.com/en/vehicles/class/e-class/wagon) right now.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


In December of 2013, I joined[The Worst Station Wagon in the World](https://www.caranddriver.com/news/a15366344/the-tale-of-the-k-it-fwd-plymouth-reliant-part-1/) and what I’m sure is[the only road-racing Checker Marathon](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/this-checker-cab-race-car-has-seen-it-all-and-it-can-now-be-yours/) on the planet for a[frozen nightmare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_North_American_winter) of a Denver-to-San Francisco road trip. That is, a nightmare for the Plymouth Reliant and Marathon drivers; I was[behind the wheel of a brand-new 2014 Mercedes-Benz E63 AMG S-Model 4MATIC W212 wagon](https://www.caranddriver.com/news/a15358460/the-long-sordid-tale-of-our-road-trip-through-frozen-hell-with-the-best-and-worst-station-wagons-in-the-world/) , and the journey was only unpleasant for me when I had to get out in -20°F weather and help fix[that wretched K-Car](https://youtu.be/eLmkGI4tMco?si=pvSTqoO7t6NOImT2&t=380) . This experience is one of the reasons why it pleases me that E-Class wagons are still being sold in the United States.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The MSRP for this sad example back in 1988 was $47,420, which comes to about $137,293[in 2026 dollars](https://murileemartin.substack.com/p/your-handy-inflationary-car-price) . You can buy[a 2027 E 450](https://www.mbusa.com/en/vehicles/model/e-class/wagon/e450s4) station wagon with all-wheel-drive and more than twice the horsepower for $80,000 (excluding destination charges and fees), which tells you a lot about the differences between E-Class shoppers now versus four decades ago.


Peugeot Motors of America


There wasn’t much direct competition for the 300 TE in the United States in 1988. The Peugeot 505 Turbo Wagon was bigger than the 300 TE and offered nearly as much horsepower for about half the price, but French cars had a not-so-great reputation here by that time. The Toyota Cressida wagon had been discontinued for the U.S. market, while the Nissan Maxima wagon was still available and a steal at $18,199, but it was smaller and had front-wheel drive. Anyone considering a Mercedes-Benz in 1988 would be unlikely to look at Detroit wagons, which leaves just the Volvo 240 and 740 wagons plus the Audi 5000 wagon… from which American car shoppers[tended to flee in terror that year](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/final-parking-space/final-parking-space-1988-audi-5000cs-turbo-quattro-sedan/) .


The Volvo 740 GLE Turbo wagon likely was the toughest 300 TE sales rival, with 160 horses going to the rear wheels, European styling, and a $25,660 price tag.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


This car drove a relatively modest total of 121,872 miles during its life. The best-traveled junkyard W124 I’ve documented was[a 1989 300 E sedan with 347,339 miles on the clock](https://www.autoblog.com/features/junkyard-gem-1989-mercedes-benz-300e-sedan-with-almost-350k-miles/) .


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The interior looked decent, if dirty, by the end.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


[MB-Tex faux-leather upholstery](https://www.capitalone.com/cars/learn/finding-the-right-car/what-is-mercedesbenz-mbtex/3013) is tougher than rhinoceros hide.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


This 300 TE drove out from Brazos County, which is Texas A&M territory, not long before it ended up in this place.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


It took some damage to the right rear at some point that I am pretty sure was close to its final day on the road, and field-expedient repairs were implemented.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


If you’re driving your Benz the 1000 miles from Brazos County to Denver, law-enforcement personnel are likely to be unhappy about a missing taillight assembly. That’s what an early-2000s Isuzu Rodeo taillight and packaging tape are for! Note the dismantler’s bar-code label still attached to the backup-lamp lens.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


I’m sure that Front Range W124 aficionados yanked some parts from this car before it perished between the cold steel jaws of[the crusher](http://www.thetruthaboutcars.com/2012/12/auction-to-crusher-12-weeks-in-the-lives-of-two-cars-at-a-self-service-wrecking-yard/) . While the W124 wagons have become tough to find in the boneyards in recent years, sedans are[still out there](https://www.row52.com/Search/?YMMorVin=YMM&Year=1985-1995&V1=&V2=&V3=&V4=&V5=&V6=&V7=&V8=&V9=&V10=&V11=&V12=&V13=&V14=&V15=&V16=&V17=&ZipCode=&Page=1&ModelId=3600&MakeId=182&LocationId=&IsVin=false&Distance=50) .


Why even *consider* some other station wagon?


When you climb into a rented W124 in North Africa, it’s like escaping from[the opening sequence of Casablanca](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K_7ITBecWmE) (except with the Germans as non-baddies). I think the[Peugeot 404 wagon](https://storm.oldcarmanualproject.com/peugeot404stationcar1967.htm) Herr Protagonist glances at in disgust would be better-suited for the local conditions, though not as good as a[504](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/final-parking-space/final-parking-space-1978-peugeot-504-diesel-sedan/) .


Do you care about the safety of your children? Well, *do you?*
